title: All Paths From Source to Target
statement: `graph` is a directed acyclic graph as an adjacency list. Nodes are 0..n-1. Return every path from 0 to n - 1, sorted lexicographically.
hints: When you reach n - 1, copy the path into the answer.
Backtrack by popping the node so sibling edges can reuse the prefix. A DAG needs no visited set.

approaches.name: BFS storing full paths
approaches.explanation: Each path is a queue item.

approaches.name: DFS backtracking
approaches.explanation: The output size dominates. The recursion depth is n.

editorial: The absence of cycles means a walk never repeats a node, so you do not need a seen set. Append the current node, recurse to each neighbor, and pop. Record a copy when the current node is the target. Sort the collected paths so the answer is unique.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def all_paths_source_target(graph: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
    target = len(graph) - 1
    out: list[list[int]] = []
    path = [0]

    def dfs(node: int) -> None:
        if node == target:
            out.append(path[:])
            return
        for nxt in graph[node]:
            path.append(nxt)
            dfs(nxt)
            path.pop()

    dfs(0)
    out.sort()
    return out
